Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with two days of lower abdominal pain, mild nausea, increased urinary frequency, feeling hot and sweaty, and pink-tinged urine; urinary tract infection (UTI) suspected, and empirical antibiotics advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal pain for two days.
- Pain is midline in lower abdomen; first occurrence of such pain.
- Associated symptoms: Mild nausea (no vomiting), feeling hot and sweaty (no measured fever, self-reported temperature 37°C), increased urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine noticed once.
- No burning or pain on urination.
- No recent diarrhoea; was constipated last week but now resolved.
- Last bowel movement two hours prior to consult, described as normal.
- Denies blood in stool.
- Denies higher abdominal pain, acid reflux, abnormal vaginal discharge, intermenstrual or post-coital bleeding.
- No back pain or malodorous urine.
- No recent travel abroad.
- No similar past episodes.
- No chills or shivering.
- Periods are regular.

Past Medical History:
- No significant medical conditions reported.
- Past illnesses limited to common cold/flu.
- No previous surgeries noted.

Medications:
- No regular prescription or over-the-counter medications.
- Previous use of contraceptive implant (removed >1 year ago).
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.

Social History:
- Lives with parents.
- Does not smoke.
- Drinks alcohol approximately four beers per week (one beer, four times per week).
- No relevant financial or lifestyle issues discussed.

Family History:
- Mother had breast cancer, treated successfully and considered early stage.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Self-reported temperature 37°C one hour prior to consult.
- No other examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- No laboratory or imaging investigations reported or performed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected urinary tract infection
  - Assessment: Two-day history of lower abdominal pain, increased urinary frequency, mild nausea, pink-tinged urine, and subjective feverishness without documented fever; no back pain or vomiting.
  - Plan:
    - Prescribe a 3-day course of antibiotics (dose/route/frequency not documented; empirical treatment discussed).
    - Advise to contact provider if pain worsens, high fever, back pain, new symptoms, or recurrence occurs.
    - Patient to start antibiotics upon collection from pharmacy.
    - Arrange follow-up if no improvement or if symptoms worsen.

General Plan:
- Ensure patient understands when to seek further care.
- Check/prioritize prompt antibiotic use and monitor for red flag symptoms.

Quality checks:

● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No medication type, dose, route, or frequency specified for antibiotics.
  - No physical examination findings except self-reported temperature.
  - No urinalysis or other investigations performed to confirm diagnosis.
  - Past surgical history not documented.
  - No allergy reaction details specified.
  - No gynecological examination/findings (if relevant to differential).
● Internal conflicts:
  - None noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Some minor hesitations, minor conversational confusion; all clinically relevant information extracted.
